title: Whole weeks, a week-by-week view, and a metric that can move
decision_task: Is the test long enough, and is the effect fading or a one-week artifact? / Which primary metric makes this test feasible inside the horizon?
business_types: any business running a split test
applies_when: gimmick-prone changes: subject lines, offers, new badges, creative
primary metric is a rare outcome (bookings, sales) at low traffic
exclusions: time-boxed events (read EXP for event tests; label as event-specific)
the proxy has no plausible link to the outcome
proxy is easily gamed (clicks via bait)
evidence_requirements: per-week counts per arm (optional but needed for the flag)
baseline for the outcome and for the candidate proxy
missing_data_behavior: Primary metric baseline unknown: keep the generous default and suggest a higher-volume step.
No weekly counts: no novelty check; label it.
alternatives_when_constrained: low traffic: compare week 1 vs the rest only, as a caution
no randomization: same weekly view on before/after, labelled observed
no instrumentation: owner notes events per week
low traffic: one bigger change, longer window, or interviews
no randomization: before/after on the proxy, labelled observed
no instrumentation: manual counts of booking clicks for 2 weeks

decision_branches.if: Primary outcome too rare to read in time
decision_branches.then: Primary = nearest feasible funnel step; outcome kept as a guardrail.

decision_branches.if: Week-1 effect much larger than later weeks
decision_branches.then: Caution: possible novelty (a label, not a verdict at small n).

implementation_steps: Lint: durationDays >= 7, warn if not a multiple of 7
At analysis: show each week's absolute change
Flag 'possible novelty' if week 1 change is more than double later weeks' change
Flag 'check data' if one week holds most conversions or a holiday/event falls in it
If flagged and reversible: extend or rerun before scaling
Size the outcome with sampleSize at its own baseline
If weeks exceed the horizon, size a nearer step (e.g. 'clicked Book now')
Use the proxy as primary, keep bookings as a guardrail/secondary read
Count only units the change can reach (triggered), and dilute by reach rate before claiming site-wide impact
If the proxy is still infeasible: before/after or qualitative path
dependencies: Baseline for the primary metric when known
observation_window: Minimum 7 days; 14+ for gimmick-prone changes (interpretation). / Whole weeks from sampleSize, within the plan horizon.
stop_conditions: novelty flag: rerun or extend before scaling
spike flag: verify data for that week
proxy up but outcome down: no ship
review_triggers: Owner corrects an input this playbook relies on
A metric or guardrail crosses its bound
The underlying source or platform rule changes
climbos_location: shared/agents/specs.ts:864 (duration), shared/analysis/decisions.ts:149 (note only), shared/growth/experimentOutcome.ts (no per-week fields) / shared/agents/specs.ts:841-843, :853-871; shared/analysis/decisions.ts:131-153

interpretation: INTERPRETATION: ExP's daily date segmentation becomes weekly at small-business volume; the flag is a caution because the per-week difference itself is not testable at this n.

INTERPRETATION: ExP's movement probability is estimated from corpora of past tests; ClimbOS can approximate it only with the baseline and MDE, so the actionable part is sizing per metric and using nearer funnel steps.
proposed_climbos_rule: PROPOSED RULE: durationDays < 7 is an error for ab_split/holdout; optional weekly counts drive novelty and spike flags.
PROPOSED RULE: size feasibility with the primary metric's baseline when known; suggest the nearest feasible funnel step otherwise.
disagreements: BK06.md:226 suggests flagging a >50% decay from week 1; at small n this will fire on noise often, so keep it a caution label.
The generous fixed baseline at specs.ts:842 is intentional ('only clearly impossible tests fail'); ExP's sensitivity framing argues it should be metric-specific when the baseline is known.
